deviations.description: ragged: selected expression of the samples of the last drug
deviations.detail: non-numeric arrays differ: 1.6.1='GEN_G055' v2='GEN_G052'; 1.6.1='GEN_G052' v2='GEN_G053'; 1.6.1='GEN_G053' v2='GEN_G049'
deviations.explanation: 1.6.1 trains one model per drug and fits the variance selection of every view inside `train` on the samples of that drug's training pairs. v2 featurizes once, on the distinct samples of all training pairs, and then splits the pairs by drug. With a drug that lacks some of the training samples (the last drug here misses the first six), the selected columns of that drug differ from the shared selection; the case compares the selected columns and values of the last drug. Measured on 2026-10-23, the two sides share 22 of 30 expression, 25 of 30 mutation and 29 of 30 copy number columns.

findings: Fixed (v2): a preset-built SuperFELTR could not finish a fit or predict, for the same reason as MOLIR: the `PredictionMode` enum in the predictor hyperparameters ended up in the Lightning checkpoints and `load_from_checkpoint` raised `UnpicklingError`. `build_components` now passes a plain string.

The networks are the 1.6.1 networks: the encoders (linear, batch norm, ReLU, dropout), the regression head and the whole `predict` path load a 1.6.1 `state_dict` with `strict=True` and agree at the `forward` class.

The regressor holds its three encoders differently. 1.6.1 keeps them in a plain tuple: they are not parameters of the module, not in its `state_dict`, and Lightning's `train()` does not reach them. v2 registers them (`nn.ModuleList`), freezes them (`requires_grad_(False)`) and overrides `train()` to keep them in eval mode. The optimizer sees only the head in both, and the encoders stay in eval mode in both, so the training agrees; the compared parameters are the head's (`regressor.*`).

1.6.1 draws the triplets of the encoder fits from an unseeded generator, v2 from the global NumPy stream seeded per fit. The case passes the same explicit seed sequence to both, in the same call order (expression, mutation and copy number encoder, drug after drug).

The encoder bias is in front of a batch norm layer, so its gradient is zero in exact arithmetic. With Adam and no weight decay the rounding noise would become full learning-rate steps (see PaccMann, SimpleNeuralNetwork); the case uses `weight_decay` 0.01 (the 1.6.1 and v2 default), which gives the bias a deterministic gradient, and continuous mutation and copy number values (a column that is constant in a batch has the same zero gradient).

Variance selection: both select the top-variance columns per view on the distinct training samples and keep the dataset column order; the expression is passed through `arcsinh` first. 1.6.1 does that while loading the CSVs (the harness applies it on the in-memory 1.6.1 side), v2 inside the featurizer. v2 fits it once over all training pairs, 1.6.1 per drug (variant `ragged`, deviation).
Neither side has a gene list: 1.6.1's `gene_lists` default is empty, the v2 preset `superfeltrOmics` names none (commit 174ceea7, B5). They agree.
